item.title: Michigan Senate: El-Sayed, Rogers Tight in Key State
item.description: Reporting from Detroit, Bloomberg News’s Romaine Bostick breaks down how Haley Stevens’s crossover endorsement is impacting the Senate battle between Mike Rogers and Abdul El-Sayed. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: What Issues Drove Voters to the Polls for Midterms?
item.description: The first polls are closing in the US midterm elections which have been dominated by voter frustration over the high cost of living. Here's what voters around the country said drove them to turn out. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Democrat Booker Wins New Jersey Senate Race, DDHQ Projects
item.description: Democratic incumbent Cory Booker is projected to win the Senate race in New Jersey, according to Decision Desk HQ on X.
item.dc:creator: Brandon Sapienza

item.title: Voting Machines Have Issues in Westchester County, NY
item.description: Voting machines in Westchester County, New York rejected paper ballots, meaning there could be a delay in determining the winner of a key US House race. Parts of Westchester County are in New York’s 17th Congressional district, one of a handful of swing seats in New York, where incumbent Republican Representative Mike Lawler has been in a tight race with Democrat Cait Conley. Bloomberg's Myles Miller reports. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Indonesia Arrests Ex-Police Chief for Allegedly Wiretapping Prabowo, Others
item.description: Indonesia’s former national police chief Listyo Sigit Prabowo and two other top police officials were arrested Tuesday for allegedly illegally wiretapping President Prabowo Subianto and other government officials.
item.dc:creator: Norman Harsono

item.title: Democrat Ossoff Projected to Win Georgia US Senate Race, DDHQ Projects
item.description: Democratic Senator Jon Ossoff is projected to win reelection in Georgia according to Ddhq. He was facing Republican Representative Mike Collins and was consistently leading in the polls. President Donald Trump's popularity in the state has been sinking due to high fuel and food prices. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Democrat Ossoff Wins Reelection in Georgia, Defeating Collins
item.description: Senator Jon Ossoff, whose speeches attacking Donald Trump for leveraging his office to grow his wealth have made him a rising Democratic star, is projected to win reelection in Georgia, sweeping aside the president’s handpicked candidate and safeguarding his party’s chances of taking control of the US Senate.
item.dc:creator: Erik Wasson

item.title: Cook Says 2026 Could Reshape the Political Map
item.description: Charlie Cook, founder and columnist with the Cook Political Report with Amy Walter, says the 2026 midterms could force a reassessment of the political map as Democrats compete beyond traditional swing states and suburban battlegrounds. Cook points to states including Ohio and Iowa as places that could become competitive again, while questioning whether the shifts emerging this year are unique to 2026 or could carry into future presidential cycles. He speaks with Joe Mathieu and Kailey Leinz on Bloomberg’s Special Election Coverage 2026. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Canada Bars Russia From Hockey Tournament Despite Arbitration Court Decision
item.description: Canada won’t allow Russian athletes to participate in a major hockey tournament that begins next month in Alberta, Prime Minister Mark Carney said, rejecting the decision of a sports tribunal.
item.dc:creator: Derek Decloet

item.title: Election Day: What to Know from Ohio
item.description: All eyes in Ohio are on two pivotal contests: the Senate race between Jon Husted and Sherrod Brown, and the governor’s race between Vivek Ramaswamy and Amy Acton. Mark Niquette reports. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Bloomberg Businessweek Daily: US Midterms Kick Off (Podcast)
item.description:
The people, companies and trends shaping the global economy. Watch Carol and Tim LIVE every day on YouTube: http://bit.ly/3vTiACF
The midterm elections have already set a record as the most expensive in US history, exceeding even the 2024 presidential race. Total spending on campaign ads this year is projected to surpass $12 billion, while more than 57 million Americans cast their ballots early. Voters say they are frustrated by the high cost of living, fuel prices that spiked after the launch of the Iran war, and uncertainty over where their jobs and the world’s largest economy are headed in the age of AI.
On today's episode:
Rick Davis, Partner at Stonecourt Capital & Bloomberg Politics Contributor Kunjan Sobhani, Bloomberg Intelligence Senior Semiconductor Analyst Wayne Sanders, Bloomberg Intelligence Senior Defense Analyst Bill Allison, Bloomberg News Campaign Finance Reporter (Source: Bloomberg)

item.description: Closing Bell Midterm Election Update Russia, China and Iran Harness AI for US Midterm Disinformation Learjet Parts Found Miles From Florida Crash Site, NTSB Says US Supreme Court Questions Arguments in Catholic Preschools’ LGBTQ+ Exclusion Case US Job Openings Jump to Four-Month High, Layoffs Decline (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Democrats Notch Early Senate Victory as US Midterm Polls Close
item.description: Polls closed in much of the country Tuesday, with Democrats securing an early win in their effort to take back the Senate after two years of President Donald Trump’s turbulent leadership.
item.dc:creator: Catherine Lucey

item.title: Midterms, Affordability & Markets
item.description: The Close brings you the latest news and analysis leading up to the final minutes and seconds before and after the closing bell on Wall Street. Today's guests are New York Life Investment Management Global Market Strategist Julia Hermann, Focus: HOPE CEO Portia Roberson, CIBC Private Wealth Senior Energy Trader Rebecca Babin, Bedrock CEO Jared Fleisher, Hamtramck City Clerk Sami Ehady, Janus Henderson Investors Head of Multi-Asset Macro Investing Mike Contopoulos, Wedbush Securities Equity Research, Hardware Managing Director Matt Bryson, VSORA Chair Sandra Rivera, S&P Global Ratings Chief Analytical Officer For Governments Nora Wittstruck, University of Michigan Surveys of Consumers Director Joanne Hsu, & Edward Jones Head of Policy, Regulatory and Government Relations Andy Blocker. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump to Watch Election Returns at White House
item.description: President Donald Trump is in the White House tonight watching the election returns. One official says Trump is feeling "cautiously optimistic." Bloomberg's Kate Sullivan reports. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Election Day: What To Know From Alaska
item.description: Voters in Alaska are choosing between incumbent Republican Dan Sullivan and Democratic challenger Mary Peltola in the Senate race. Anna Edgerton reports (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Russia Tries Return to World Juniors in Canada as Sweden, Finland Refuse to Play
item.description: Plus: America’s referendum on Trump’s second term
item.dc:creator: Derek Decloet and Laura Osman

item.title: Court Backs DOJ in Fight Over Pressuring Election Officials
item.description: A federal appeals court cleared the Trump administration to potentially resume pressuring state and local election officials to prevent voting by people it claims may be noncitizens as Americans go to the polls in the midterm elections.
item.dc:creator: Zoe Tillman, Greg Stohr and Erik Larson

item.title: Voting Machines Falter as Westchester Decides Key New York House Race
item.description: Election officials in New York’s Westchester County were racing to address an issue that caused voting machines to reject paper ballots, a snafu that raised the possibility of delays in determining the winner of a key US House race.
item.dc:creator: Laura Nahmias, Cameron Fozi and Nacha Cattan

item.title: US, Iran Pursue Diplomacy Despite Limited American Strikes
item.description: Tehran and Washington are reviewing fresh proposals from mediators on how to resolve their differences and avoid a return to all-out war, according to a diplomat briefed on the matter, after limited US airstrikes overnight.
item.dc:creator: Fiona MacDonald and Ahmed Elimam
